title: RTFL: Energy-Aware Federated Learning for AIoT Design Via Adaptive Quantization-Based Multi-Agent Scheduling
evidence_span: RTFL uses adaptive-quantization multi-agent scheduling to select devices and model quantization levels per federated-learning round, accounting for battery, compute, and bandwidth; the official description reports faster convergence and more aggregation participation but supplies no numeric values or device/training configuration.
problem: Battery-powered AIoT federated learning suffers from slow convergence and poor training performance under heterogeneous compute and communication resources.
method_or_artifact: Multi-agent reinforcement-learning scheduler with adaptive quantization and device selection under a training-time constraint.
workload_or_benchmark: Federated learning across resource-constrained AIoT devices; dataset, model, device population, rounds, and convergence metric are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Heterogeneous battery-powered devices with varying compute, residual energy, and communication bandwidth; radio and processor details are unspecified.
limits: No convergence curves, accuracy, energy budget, communication volume, agent count, or baseline configuration are supplied.
More participation may trade off energy, fairness, and model quality across devices.
Official description only; training and scheduling claims require paper-level verification.

title: GPU-Fuzz: Finding Memory Errors in Deep Learning Frameworks
evidence_span: GPU-Fuzz models operator parameters as formal constraints and uses a constraint solver to generate boundary-focused tests for GPU kernels; applied to PyTorch, TensorFlow, and PaddlePaddle, the official description reports 13 previously unknown bugs.
problem: GPU memory errors in deep-learning frameworks can cause crashes and security issues, while ordinary fuzzing may miss structured boundary conditions in operators.
method_or_artifact: Constraint-based GPU-kernel fuzzer that formalizes operator parameters and systematically generates boundary-condition test cases.
workload_or_benchmark: PyTorch, TensorFlow, and PaddlePaddle GPU operators; tested operator inventory, GPU architectures, execution budget, and bug-severity criteria are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: GPU kernels executed through major deep-learning frameworks; GPU models, drivers, compiler versions, and sanitizer configuration are unspecified.
limits: The description omits fuzzing duration, operator coverage, deduplication, bug confirmation process, and baseline discovery counts.
Unknown-bug counts are sensitive to framework versions and disclosure/triage policies.
Official description only; reproducibility and security impact require paper-level verification.

title: Drcagent: A Design Rule Aware LLM Agent for DRC Auto-Fix with Adversarial Reinforcement Learning
evidence_span: drcAgent combines a multimodal LLM with retrieval from a design-rule knowledge graph and self-play adversarial reinforcement learning between Generator and Fixer agents, using commercial EDA tools for interaction; industrial-scale cases demonstrate effective violation fixing, but no numeric closure or quality values are supplied.
problem: Leading-edge DRC violations have complex geometry and rule dependencies that make template or heuristic correction difficult to adapt across process nodes.
method_or_artifact: RAG-grounded multimodal LLM agent, design-rule knowledge graph, and adversarial multi-turn reinforcement-learning loop with EDA-tool feedback.
workload_or_benchmark: Industrial-scale physical-design DRC correction; process node, rule deck, violation classes, starting violation counts, and closure criteria are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Commercial EDA DRC tools and leading-edge design rules at approximately 7 nm and below; foundry, layout size, runtime, and licensing conditions are unspecified.
limits: No violation-closure rate, design-rule coverage, runtime, layout-quality impact, or process portability is supplied.
Commercial-tool interaction and proprietary rule data may constrain reproducibility.
Official description only; correction validity and adversarial-training behavior require paper-level verification.

title: M²CAM: A Multi-Level Memristor-Based Self-Adaptive CAM Architecture for Genome Processing Acceleration
evidence_span: M²CAM uses multi-level memristor conductance states for analog CAM nucleotide encoding and a self-adaptive error-correction mechanism that changes matching precision under device variation; on real single-cell RNA-sequencing data, the official description reports 50–75% lower device use, 131.2–3088.9x energy improvement, and 161.2–269.6x latency improvement over CPU/GPU and STAR baselines.
problem: Genome sequence matching and classification are limited by data movement and bandwidth, while digital encodings impose area and parallelism overhead in in-memory genome accelerators.
method_or_artifact: Multi-level memristor analog CAM, hierarchical precision adaptation for variation tolerance, and parallel genome-classification framework.
workload_or_benchmark: Single-cell RNA sequencing datasets and genome sequence matching/classification; dataset sizes, sequence lengths, accuracy/recall, and device-variation distributions are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Multi-level memristor conductance states and analog CAM arrays; device technology, ADC/DAC, precision, endurance, and peripheral overhead are unspecified.
limits: The wide improvement ranges lack matched hardware, tool, dataset, and accuracy conditions.
Analog peripheral, calibration, endurance, and variation costs may materially change system-level results.
Official description only; biological accuracy and measured-device claims require paper-level verification.

title: Memflow: Characterizing Memory Traffic Contention in Disaggregated Architectures
evidence_span: MemFlow provides modular, fine-grained abstractions for pooled disaggregated processors and memories, traces the complete load/store path through queues, caches, and memory controllers, and supports design-space exploration for contention mitigation; the official description emphasizes fidelity but reports no numeric validation or mitigation gains.
problem: Any-processor-to-any-memory traffic in scale-up disaggregated systems creates contention across microarchitectural components that simplified simulators fail to represent.
method_or_artifact: Flow-centric simulator with detailed memory-path abstractions and automated exploration of contention-mitigation designs.
workload_or_benchmark: Disaggregated processor/memory traffic and scale-up network workloads; traces, processor count, memory topology, validation targets, and simulator baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Pooled disaggregated memory connected through a scale-up network, with load-store queues, cache hierarchies, and memory controllers; link and protocol details are unspecified.
baselines: existing disaggregated-memory simulators with simplified paths
metrics: Fine-grained contention characterization and design-space exploration claimed qualitatively
limits: No validation error, simulation speed, workload suite, contention metrics, or mitigation results are supplied.
Detailed modeling may trade simulation cost against fidelity and may depend on unavailable proprietary network parameters.
Official description only; simulator implementation and validation require paper-level verification.
